# Wave 21 - the parallel panel (R11): acceptance brief

Commit under review: 2de15e9 (main), on top of d6f3514 (design + decisions). Design:
handoffs/01-claude-r11-design.md. Binding decisions: handoffs/05-claude-r11-decisions.md (D1-D13).
This very review runs through the new code: the members of this panel run concurrently.

## What wave 21 implements (per the implementer's report)

- `codex-consult-common.ps1`: new `Get-PanelPlan` (endpoint groups: labels sharing a provider
  fingerprint or the agy sign-in are merged, a merged group takes the smallest `parallel` limit),
  `Get-PanelIgnorePrefixes` (D7, incl. Write-TextAtomic temp names), `Enter-WriteLock` /
  `Get-WriteLockTimeout`, the single store-commit routine `Enter-StoreCommit` /
  `Complete-StoreCommit` / `Exit-StoreCommit`, `Add-LedgerEntry` (insert by n),
  `Get-MemberPendingPath`, `Get-PendingPaths`, `Read-TaskPendingRecords`. Changed:
  `Get-NextNumbers` (array of leftovers), `Add-ReplyFindings` (findings kept in id order),
  `Get-EndpointHealth` (`finished_at`, else `when` + `wall_seconds`, ties by n),
  `Read-ReviewerRoster` (top-level `parallel`), `Enter-TaskLock -Panel`, `New-PendingRecord`
  (`start_time`, `panel`), `Test-PendingActive` (live writer = active; member records never use the
  name rule; state `committing`).
- `codex-consult.ps1`: `-PanelConcurrency`; member proof and record rewrite (D6/D1); members skip
  the lock, the recovery pass and numbering; parent re-check before `launching`; the panel parent
  rewritten (lock held throughout, all records judged, numbers up front, records before launch,
  Start-Process + 500 ms polling, guard, cleanup, summary with the panel's wall clock); commit
  restructured (`committing`, give-up path, ingest and render inside the lock, `finished_at`);
  `sessions.json` is no longer created at run start (the commit creates it).
- `codex-findings.ps1`: lists every record; `-Status` checks all records; `-Status` and `-Rate`
  write through the store commit.
- Tests: new `tests/harness-panel.ps1` (48 assertions: plan, overlap, order by n, no lost update
  under contention, in-flight refusals, member timeout, sequential cap, agy sibling writes,
  parent killed, spec proof, commit blocked, ORPHAN on a kill inside the commit, guard kill); the
  full suite is green under Windows PowerShell 5.1, harness-panel also under pwsh 7.6.6.

## Deviations the implementer declared

1. Labels resolving to one provider fingerprint (and all agy labels) form one sequential group.
2. `sessions.json` is created by the first commit, not at run start.
3. `findings.json` is kept in id order.
4. Ledger `panel.concurrency` = the most members the plan lets run at once; `limits` per label.
5. The member's record rewrite happens after in-memory validation, roster read and repo-root
   resolution (nothing touches the task before it).
6. "Descendants of the writer" is the existing ppid rule over the writer and recorded pids; outside
   Windows member records are judged by recorded pids only.
7. Test hooks `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_WRITE_LOCK_SEC`, `_COMMIT_PAUSE_MS`, `_PANEL_GUARD_SEC`.

## Residuals the implementer declared

- If the parent dies between a member's parent check and its record rewrite, a new run may consume
  that record; the member recreates it and runs beside the new run with distinct numbers (commits
  stay safe under the write lock).
- Outside Windows, a member record whose recorded pids are all dead cannot find an orphaned
  reviewer (no ppid rule there, and D1 forbids the name rule).
- A guard-killed member's short-lived orphan child (e.g. git) can make the next run refuse briefly.
- The member spec is still base64 on the command line (32767-character limit on long prompts).

## The ask

1. For every open finding listed in your prompt (F02-*, F03-*, F04-*): fixed / still open /
   accepted limitation per the decisions - with the code location that shows it.
2. New defects in the implemented concurrency, recovery and commit paths, the plan, the member
   proof, the agy ignore list, `codex-findings.ps1` and the tests' ability to catch regressions.
   Cite lines of 2de15e9. Say what you verified in code and what you inferred.
3. ACCEPT only if no blocker or major remains; HOLD names exactly what must change.

# R11 - decisions after the design review (round 1)

Reviews: 02 kimi :: k3 (ADVISE, F02-1..5), 03 byteplus :: deepseek-v4.1-flash (ADVISE, F03-1..11),
04 ZAI :: glm-5.3 (ADVISE, F04-1..8). All three accept member-side commit under a write lock (Q1);
none accepts the recovery model as written. The design in 01 stands where not overridden here.

D1. Liveness of every recovery record includes its WRITER (F03-1, F02-1, F04-4, F03-2, F04-5).
    Records carry the writing bridge's `pid` + `start_time`. A member rewrites the record the parent
    wrote for it with its own pid + start time as its first act. `Test-PendingActive`: a live writer
    (pid + matching start time) makes a record ACTIVE in every state, `reserved` included. For panel
    member records (a `panel` field) activity is judged ONLY by recorded pids + start times (writer,
    child, survivors) and, on Windows, by descendants of the recorded writer pid - never by the
    machine-wide name rule. Non-panel records keep today's rules plus the writer check.
    New state `committing`, written before the member takes the write lock. A member re-checks its
    parent (pid + start time) right before `launching` and stops there, nothing started, when the
    parent is gone.

D2. The write lock is an OS-held handle (F03-5a, F04-3). `<task>/.consult.write.lock`, permanent
    file, never unlinked, opened exclusively like `Enter-TaskLock` (release = close; a killed holder
    releases it). ONE shared routine "take write lock -> re-read stores -> apply delta -> write ->
    release" is used by panel members, single runs AND `codex-findings.ps1` (status changes,
    ratings), so no writer ever writes a store snapshot read before the lock.

D3. Give-up never touches the stores (F04-2, F02-4). Write lock not acquired within 60 s (retry
    with backoff): the member keeps its record in state `committing` with a note naming the reply
    files, keeps reply.json / events / the raw reply, exits non-zero, and the panel summary names it
    "commit blocked". The next run consumes the record like any interrupted reservation (numbering
    skips it) and names the orphaned reply (the `Get-PendingOriginalNote` flow).

D4. Ingest and render inside the lock (F03-6). Order: reply.json (before the lock) -> lock ->
    re-read -> `Add-ReplyFindings` on the fresh store -> handoff .md rendered from THAT ingest ->
    findings.json -> sessions.json (entry inserted by n) -> remove record -> release. A kill inside
    the lock can still leave ORPHAN findings (F03-11): accepted and documented; harness case added.

D5. Multiple leftovers (F02-3, F03-7). `Get-NextNumbers` takes an array of leftover records (max
    n / NN over all, per-record Recovered). Every reader enumerates `.consult.pending*.json`
    (`codex-consult.ps1`, `codex-findings.ps1 -List/-Status`). At the summary the parent removes
    the records of members it never launched and of launched members that are gone with the record
    still `reserved` (nothing was started).

D6. Member proof without the lock file (F03-5b). A member accepts its spec only when its own
    per-member record (written by the parent before the launch) names the same panel id, n, NN and
    parent pid + start time, and that parent is alive. Otherwise it refuses with a message naming
    the mismatch; nothing started.

D7. agy tree check (F04-1; F02-2 accepted). For a member of a concurrent panel the collab comparison
    also ignores the Write-TextAtomic temp variant of every ignored path (`.<name>.<guid>.tmp` in the
    same directory as `sessions.json`, `findings.json`, a sibling's `handoffs/<NN>-*`). The
    whole-collab-root scope stays (wave 18): a run on ANOTHER task committing during an agy run
    fails that run - pre-existing, now documented as a residual; do not run other tasks beside a
    panel with agy members.

D8. Endpoint-aware concurrency (F03-4, F04-8). Members run in parallel across provider labels and
    one after another within a label (all entries of one label share an endpoint or a sign-in; agy
    entries share the Google sign-in). The roster may raise a label's limit: an optional top-level
    `"parallel": { "<provider label>": <n> }` (validated: integers >= 1, labels present in the
    roster). `-PanelConcurrency <n>` is a global cap on top (0 = none, the default; 1 = strictly one
    after another, where the F15-3 "later members not started" rule still applies). Dry run and
    the ledger `panel` record show the effective plan (`concurrency`, the per-label limits).

D9. Completion time for health (F03-3, F02-5). Ledger entries gain `finished_at` (ISO, written at
    commit). `Get-EndpointHealth` orders by `finished_at` (older entries: `when` + `wall_seconds`),
    ties broken by n.

D10. Order invariant (F04-7, F03-9). `consults` stays sorted by n. Inside one panel a lineage
     appears once (same provider + model is refused), and across runs the task lock serialises
     lineages, so "highest n of a lineage = newest thread" holds; `Select-ParentThread` unchanged.
     Stated in README and asserted by a harness case (slowest member first in roster order).

D11. Guard from the spec (F04-6). The parent's kill guard for a member = its timeout + the format
     repair and denial retry budgets (when enabled) + 60 s write lock + 120 s slack.

D12. Task lock for the whole panel stays (F03-8 accepted as a limitation): `codex-findings.ps1`
     writes are refused while a panel runs, as a single run refuses them today. D2 makes relaxing
     this later (R12) safe. Documented.

D13. Fakes (F03-10): a per-model delay map and per-model reply for fake-codex3 (keyed by `-m`) and a
     delay for fake-agy, before the panel cases.

Important observations so far:

1. `Get-PanelIgnorePrefixes` returns an EMPTY list when `$nns.Count -eq 0` — meaning if the panel effectively runs one member at a time (concurrency 1, or a single-member group), the store prefixes are NOT ignored. Wait, but the store prefixes should always be ignored for a panel member, because the member itself writes them? No — the member's own store writes happen at commit, after the tree check. Hmm, but the check happens... let me re-check when the agy tree check occurs relative to commit. In HEAD, treeProblem is computed at 2155/2439 (before commit). With wave 21, "commit restructured". Need to check whether the collab after-snapshot is taken before or after the commit. If the after-snapshot is taken before commit, the member's own store writes are not in the window, so only siblings' writes matter → ignoring stores only when siblings exist is right. OK, that's defensible.

But careful: `$SiblingNns` — when is it empty? "none when the panel runs one member at a time" — i.e., the parent decides. Need to check the caller. If the panel has 1 runner... Also note: if the panel is concurrent, the sibling NNs must include only siblings that could be writing concurrently. Need to check the parent's computation.

Also: `Get-PanelIgnorePrefixes` adds `"$Task/$store"` as a *prefix* — `Task/sessions.json` prefix also matches `Task/sessions.json.something`, fine. But it does NOT include the member's OWN handoff writes — those are handled by OwnPrefixes elsewhere (existing mechanism).

Critical: the ignore list does NOT include `.consult.pending-<NN>.json` / `.consult.write.lock` / `.consult.lock` — those are skipped by Get-CollabSnapshot's `.consult.` name filter. What about the atomic temp of a pending file: `..consult.pending-07.json.<guid>.tmp` — starts with `..consult.` → skipped (the filter covers `..consult.` prefix). Good.

But what about the members' `handoffs/<NN>-codex-...reply.json` etc.? Covered by `$Task/handoffs/$s-`.

What about `handoffs/.<NN>-....tmp` (atomic temp for the handoff file, created by Write-Utf8NoBom→Write-TextAtomic?). The `.gitignore` shows `..consult.*`. The prefix `"$Task/handoffs/.$s-"` covers `Task/handoffs/.07-codex-x-openai.md.<guid>.tmp`. Good.

But: does the member write its handoff via Write-TextAtomic? If the temp name is `.<name>.<guid>.tmp` then covered. Let me verify Write-TextAtomic's temp naming: earlier comment said "the atomic-write temp `..consult.*`". Let me read Write-TextAtomic (line 119 area) to know the temp naming convention precisely, since F04-1's claim depends on it. In the previous review I noted `.sessions.json.<guid>.tmp`. Let me check.

2. `Enter-WriteLock` retries only on `[System.IO.IOException]`. On Windows, opening a file held with FileShare.Read and requesting ReadWrite access throws IOException — good. Also `FileShare.Read` on the holder means a second opener requesting ReadWrite fails. Good. The judgement `catch [System.IO.IOException]` → retry. And the give-up message includes Waited. OK.

Note: `Enter-WriteLock` writes its informational record into the file it holds — meaning the RECORD write happens while holding, like Enter-TaskLock. But: `Enter-WriteLock`'s `$record` has no `panel` field... fine.

Potential defect: `Exit-TaskLock -Lock $Commit.Lock` in Exit-StoreCommit — Exit-TaskLock checks `$Lock.Acquired`. Enter-WriteLock returns `$r` (New-LockRefusal) on failure which has Acquired=$false. In Enter-StoreCommit, if not acquired, is Exit-TaskLock called? Let me read the truncated part of Enter-StoreCommit. Need full text.

# Wave 21 - the parallel panel (R11): acceptance brief

Commit under review: 2de15e9 (main), on top of d6f3514 (design + decisions). Design:
handoffs/01-claude-r11-design.md. Binding decisions: handoffs/05-claude-r11-decisions.md (D1-D13).
This very review runs through the new code: the members of this panel run concurrently.

## What wave 21 implements (per the implementer's report)

- `codex-consult-common.ps1`: new `Get-PanelPlan` (endpoint groups: labels sharing a provider
  fingerprint or the agy sign-in are merged, a merged group takes the smallest `parallel` limit),
  `Get-PanelIgnorePrefixes` (D7, incl. Write-TextAtomic temp names), `Enter-WriteLock` /
  `Get-WriteLockTimeout`, the single store-commit routine `Enter-StoreCommit` /
  `Complete-StoreCommit` / `Exit-StoreCommit`, `Add-LedgerEntry` (insert by n),
  `Get-MemberPendingPath`, `Get-PendingPaths`, `Read-TaskPendingRecords`. Changed:
  `Get-NextNumbers` (array of leftovers), `Add-ReplyFindings` (findings kept in id order),
  `Get-EndpointHealth` (`finished_at`, else `when` + `wall_seconds`, ties by n),
  `Read-ReviewerRoster` (top-level `parallel`), `Enter-TaskLock -Panel`, `New-PendingRecord`
  (`start_time`, `panel`), `Test-PendingActive` (live writer = active; member records never use the
  name rule; state `committing`).
- `codex-consult.ps1`: `-PanelConcurrency`; member proof and record rewrite (D6/D1); members skip
  the lock, the recovery pass and numbering; parent re-check before `launching`; the panel parent
  rewritten (lock held throughout, all records judged, numbers up front, records before launch,
  Start-Process + 500 ms polling, guard, cleanup, summary with the panel's wall clock); commit
  restructured (`committing`, give-up path, ingest and render inside the lock, `finished_at`);
  `sessions.json` is no longer created at run start (the commit creates it).
- `codex-findings.ps1`: lists every record; `-Status` checks all records; `-Status` and `-Rate`
  write through the store commit.
- Tests: new `tests/harness-panel.ps1` (48 assertions: plan, overlap, order by n, no lost update
  under contention, in-flight refusals, member timeout, sequential cap, agy sibling writes,
  parent killed, spec proof, commit blocked, ORPHAN on a kill inside the commit, guard kill); the
  full suite is green under Windows PowerShell 5.1, harness-panel also under pwsh 7.6.6.

## Deviations the implementer declared

1. Labels resolving to one provider fingerprint (and all agy labels) form one sequential group.
2. `sessions.json` is created by the first commit, not at run start.
3. `findings.json` is kept in id order.
4. Ledger `panel.concurrency` = the most members the plan lets run at once; `limits` per label.
5. The member's record rewrite happens after in-memory validation, roster read and repo-root
   resolution (nothing touches the task before it).
6. "Descendants of the writer" is the existing ppid rule over the writer and recorded pids; outside
   Windows member records are judged by recorded pids only.
7. Test hooks `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_WRITE_LOCK_SEC`, `_COMMIT_PAUSE_MS`, `_PANEL_GUARD_SEC`.

## Residuals the implementer declared

- If the parent dies between a member's parent check and its record rewrite, a new run may consume
  that record; the member recreates it and runs beside the new run with distinct numbers (commits
  stay safe under the write lock).
- Outside Windows, a member record whose recorded pids are all dead cannot find an orphaned
  reviewer (no ppid rule there, and D1 forbids the name rule).
- A guard-killed member's short-lived orphan child (e.g. git) can make the next run refuse briefly.
- The member spec is still base64 on the command line (32767-character limit on long prompts).

## The ask

1. For every open finding listed in your prompt (F02-*, F03-*, F04-*): fixed / still open /
   accepted limitation per the decisions - with the code location that shows it.
2. New defects in the implemented concurrency, recovery and commit paths, the plan, the member

   Cite lines of 2de15e9. Say what you verified in code and what you inferred.
3. ACCEPT only if no blocker or major remains; HOLD names exactly what must change.

F02-4's remedy... The design item 6 said "recorded as a bridge failure, reply files kept". The implementer instead keeps the record with reply_json. Fine — an improvement, observable. I'll call F02-4 fixed with that nuance (the reply is never ingested; it must be ingested by hand — documented in README? maybe). Acceptable.

README documents the residual (1200-1207). F02-2 → accepted limitation per D7, documented.

Now, an important observation about F04-1 (temp files): `Get-CollabSnapshot` at 645 skips names starting with `.consult.` or `..consult.` — the Write-TextAtomic temp for `sessions.json` is `.sessions.json.<guid>.tmp` (starts with `.sessions.json.`), so it's NOT skipped by 645 — hence the D7 ignore prefixes add `$Task/.sessions.json.` and `$Task/.findings.json.`. And the handoff temp `.<NN>-...` is covered by `$Task/handoffs/.$s-`. So F04-1 fixed. BUT: the temp files are created for `reply.json`/`events`/`.md` inside handoffs — covered by `$Task/handoffs/.$s-`. And `.consult.pending-<NN>.json` temps are skipped at 645. Good.

Hmm, but what about the member's *own* writes to `<task>/handoffs/<its own NN>-...`? Those are ignored as the member's own files (the caller's own prefixes). Let me verify what ignore prefixes the agy member passes for itself: at 2308 `$siblingPrefixes` — and presumably own files are added separately. Let me check the call site of Compare-DirectorySnapshot in codex-consult.ps1 (~2439) and how own prefixes are built.

Let me look at 2420-2460.

Own prefixes: `"$Task/handoffs/$nn-$enginePrefix-$ReplyName."` — the own handoff (with the reply name suffix). Note the agy member's own files: `handoffs/<nn>-agy-<replyname>.md`, `.events.jsonl`, `.reply.json` — covered by the prefix `...-<ReplyName>.` — yes since files are `NN-agy-<ReplyName>.md` etc.

Hmm, subtle: the member's own prefix uses `$ReplyName` which for a member is "$ReplyName-$slug" (e.g. `c-openai`), so the file is `01-agy-c-openai.md` and the prefix `$Task/handoffs/01-agy-c-openai.` matches. Good.

Now — one real gap: the panel's *parent* also writes into the task dir while members run? The parent writes nothing during the run (records written before launch; removed after all members finish at 1299-1310). Good — that's why records-before-launch was chosen.

But wait: at 1303-1305, the parent removes the unused `reserved` records for members in state waiting/blocked/failed-start — after all members finish. Fine, and `Get-CollabSnapshot` skips `.consult.pending-*`. Good.

Now the agy member's after-snapshot: does the member take the after-snapshot after its reviewer exits, i.e. could a sibling's commit land between the agy member's before and after snapshots in a path not ignored? The ignored paths are the two stores + siblings' handoffs. A sibling's commit writes: findings.json, sessions.json, handoffs/<NN>-...md, temperature files. All covered. Plus the sibling might write:
- `handoffs/<NN>-...reply.json` (written earlier, before the commit — could land during the agy member's run window; covered by the sibling prefix).
- `handoffs/<NN>-...events.jsonl` — covered.
- What about the sibling's *record* file `.consult.pending-<NN>.json` — skipped by name rule.
- `codex-findings.ps1 -List` writes nothing.
- Hmm: does the member write anything else, e.g. `.collab/<task>/<something>`? `Find-ThreadInRollouts` reads CODEX_HOME. Fine.

OK. So the design is well-covered. Now: the *parent* holds the task lock, so cross-task runs are the only concurrency allowed — D7's limitation.

Now let me make a decision. So far I've found no blocker. My handoff summary's "blocker" appears to be based on a misreading. But I should be careful: maybe there IS a genuine issue with the `committing` state on **non-Windows**: line 5184-5187 returns inactive for a panel record *regardless of the writer check*? No — the writer check at 5146 comes first, so a live writer → active. Good. So on Linux, a member in its commit window with a live bridge process is ACTIVE. So F03-1/F02-1's "commit window" hole: is it really fixed? The record's writer (pid) is the member's bridge process, which stays alive through the commit → ACTIVE while committing. Yes: fixed. Good — that's the D1 design.

Wait, but what about the window *after* the member's bridge exits but before... no, the record removal happens before the bridge exits (3142 < exit). Fine.

Hmm, but one more: the writer check requires `$writerStart` (start_time) and `$writerPid -ne $PID`. The member sets both. And `Test-PidAlive -ProcessId -StartTime` presumably compares the recorded start time with the live process's start time to guard pid reuse. Good.

Now, what about the parent's own record? A panel run does NOT write `.consult.pending.json` for itself. So while a panel runs, the task has only member records. If the panel parent dies, the members are the records. Fine.

OK — so maybe the honest verdict is ACCEPT, with a couple of minor/major findings about test coverage and documentation drift. But the brief says "ACCEPT only if no blocker or major remains". Are test-coverage gaps "major"? The acceptance ask #3: "HOLD names exactly what must change". A missing regression test for a declared residual (ORPHAN in a panel member) is arguably minor, not major.

Hmm, but let me hunt a bit more for a genuine bug in areas I haven't looked at: `Get-PanelMemberStatus`, `Find-PanelEntry`, and `-PanelAll`/`-Panel` argument validation (e.g. `-Panel` with `-PanelConcurrency`), and the `Test-PendingActive` doc/authorization for `reserved`+live-writer (an inconsistency I noted: doc says reserved is never active, code returns active for a live writer). Which is right? Consider a *single* run: it writes `.consult.pending.json` with state 'reserved' *before* launching codex, while it holds the task lock. Another run can't be running. So it doesn't matter. For a panel: records are `reserved` while the parent lives → active → good for -Status refusals? Actually `codex-findings -List` (no lock) just prints. And a *new run* would be refused by the task lock anyway.

Hmm, but here's a thought: after the panel parent dies, the `reserved` records (members never started) have `pid` = dead parent → inactive → consumed. Good, matches D5's cleanup.

Let me now check one more potentially serious thing: **the member's `Test-PendingActive` is used by the parent for the `-PanelConcurrency 1` rule on the *finished* member's record** — where the record was removed but the *member's reviewer* might still be a survivor... Covered by design.

Let me look for a bug in the *interaction between the write lock and the task lock for codex-findings -Rate*: at 428-431 `finally { Exit-StoreCommit; Exit-TaskLock }` — but the -Rate block: does it take the task lock? Let me check around 373-400 to see the lock acquisition. If -Rate takes the write lock but *not* the task lock, then a -Rate could interleave with a panel member's commit — protected by the write lock anyway. Fine either way. But the F04-3 check "grep for a single commit function used by members, single runs and codex-findings alike" → done.

Let me now check the -Rate path's lock ordering for deadlock potential: if -Rate takes the task lock then the write lock → consistent order everywhere (task → write). Members take only write. OK.

At this point I have enough for a thorough review. But hold on — I should double check one potentially real MAJOR: `Get-NextNumbers`'s `$maxN = @($Consults).Count` combined with the panel's up-front allocation of n = N+k-1. The panel's *members* each get n. But the panel parent *also* reserves nothing for itself. Fine.

The design's residual covers the pre-rewrite window. What about this: after the parent dies, a *new run* starts *while a member is committing*. The new run reads the member's record: state `committing`, writer = the member's pid → ALIVE → refused. Good, tested? Not tested, but code-correct.

**Scenario Y: a member's `Write-PendingFile` (record rewrite at 884-890) racing the parent's `Write-PendingFile` for the same path?** The parent writes all records before launching, and never writes a member's record again (it only removes unused ones). Good.

But the *consumed* record's number is skipped. Fine.

Hmm, what about `maxN` from the *ledger entry count*: `$maxN = @($Consults).Count`. Suppose a panel's members commit in a different order and a *lower-n* entry's n > count? Not possible since n values are dense-ish. Fine.

**Scenario W: two panels on the same task at once?** The second panel takes the task lock → refused. Fine.

**Scenario V: `-Panel` while a leftover `.consult.pending.json` is active → refused. Fine.

**Scenario U: `codex-findings.ps1 -Rate` doesn't read pending records (only -Status does).** Is that a real risk? `-Rate` takes the task lock first. If a panel is running, the task lock refuses. If the parent died and a member is alive in its commit, `-Rate` takes the free task lock, then the *write lock* — which the member holds during its commit → `-Rate` waits (60 s default) → then gives up with "nothing was changed" (exit 1). So no corruption; just a possible 60 s stall. Fine, not a defect worth filing beyond a note.

Hmm, actually there's one more thing: `-Rate` at 453/481 uses `Enter-StoreCommit -NoSessions`? Let me check -Rate's Enter-StoreCommit call — at 391-400ish. If -Rate writes findings.json only and reads sessions under the lock but never writes sessions, fine.

So the member's verdict is measured against the baseline, deliberately. The stored finding's `reviewer_checks` get appended (id-ordered). (minor) `Get-PanelIgnorePrefixes` ignores *every* sibling's handoff prefix whenever the plan is >1, not only members that can actually overlap in time; a member that finishes and commits much later... hmm, actually with groups, siblings in *other* groups can overlap. # R11 - decisions after the design review (round 1)

Reviews: 02 kimi :: k3 (ADVISE, F02-1..5), 03 byteplus :: deepseek-v4.1-flash (ADVISE, F03-1..11),
04 ZAI :: glm-5.3 (ADVISE, F04-1..8). All three accept member-side commit under a write lock (Q1);
none accepts the recovery model as written. The design in 01 stands where not overridden here.

D1. Liveness of every recovery record includes its WRITER (F03-1, F02-1, F04-4, F03-2, F04-5).
    Records carry the writing bridge's `pid` + `start_time`. A member rewrites the record the parent
    wrote for it with its own pid + start time as its first act. `Test-PendingActive`: a live writer
    (pid + matching start time) makes a record ACTIVE in every state, `reserved` included. For panel
    member records (a `panel` field) activity is judged ONLY by recorded pids + start times (writer,
    child, survivors) and, on Windows, by descendants of the recorded writer pid - never by the
    machine-wide name rule. Non-panel records keep today's rules plus the writer check.
    New state `committing`, written before the member takes the write lock. A member re-checks its
    parent (pid + start time) right before `launching` and stops there, nothing started, when the
    parent is gone.

D2. The write lock is an OS-held handle (F03-5a, F04-3). `<task>/.consult.write.lock`, permanent
    file, never unlinked, opened exclusively like `Enter-TaskLock` (release = close; a killed holder
    releases it). ONE shared routine "take write lock -> re-read stores -> apply delta -> write ->
    release" is used by panel members, single runs AND `codex-findings.ps1` (status changes,
    ratings), so no writer ever writes a store snapshot read before the lock.

D3. Give-up never touches the stores (F04-2, F02-4). Write lock not acquired within 60 s (retry
    with backoff): the member keeps its record in state `committing` with a note naming the reply
    files, keeps reply.json / events / the raw reply, exits non-zero, and the panel summary names it
    "commit blocked". The next run consumes the record like any interrupted reservation (numbering
    skips it) and names the orphaned reply (the `Get-PendingOriginalNote` flow).

D4. Ingest and render inside the lock (F03-6). Order: reply.json (before the lock) -> lock ->
    re-read -> `Add-ReplyFindings` on the fresh store -> handoff .md rendered from THAT ingest ->
    findings.json -> sessions.json (entry inserted by n) -> remove record -> release. A kill inside
    the lock can still leave ORPHAN findings (F03-11): accepted and documented; harness case added.

D5. Multiple leftovers (F02-3, F03-7). `Get-NextNumbers` takes an array of leftover records (max
    n / NN over all, per-record Recovered). Every reader enumerates `.consult.pending*.json`
    (`codex-consult.ps1`, `codex-findings.ps1 -List/-Status`). At the summary the parent removes
    the records of members it never launched and of launched members that are gone with the record
    still `reserved` (nothing was started).

D6. Member proof without the lock file (F03-5b). A member accepts its spec only when its own
    per-member record (written by the parent before the launch) names the same panel id, n, NN and
    parent pid + start time, and that parent is alive. Otherwise it refuses with a message naming
    the mismatch; nothing started.

D7. agy tree check (F04-1; F02-2 accepted). For a member of a concurrent panel the collab comparison
    also ignores the Write-TextAtomic temp variant of every ignored path (`.<name>.<guid>.tmp` in the
    same directory as `sessions.json`, `findings.json`, a sibling's `handoffs/<NN>-*`). The
    whole-collab-root scope stays (wave 18): a run on ANOTHER task committing during an agy run
    fails that run - pre-existing, now documented as a residual; do not run other tasks beside a
    panel with agy members.

D8. Endpoint-aware concurrency (F03-4, F04-8). Members run in parallel across provider labels and
    one after another within a label (all entries of one label share an endpoint or a sign-in; agy
    entries share the Google sign-in). The roster may raise a label's limit: an optional top-level
    `"parallel": { "<provider label>": <n> }` (validated: integers >= 1, labels present in the
    roster). `-PanelConcurrency <n>` is a global cap on top (0 = none, the default; 1 = strictly one
    after another, where the F15-3 "later members not started" rule still applies). Dry run and
    the ledger `panel` record show the effective plan (`concurrency`, the per-label limits).

D9. Completion time for health (F03-3, F02-5). Ledger entries gain `finished_at` (ISO, written at
    commit). `Get-EndpointHealth` orders by `finished_at` (older entries: `when` + `wall_seconds`),
    ties broken by n.

D10. Order invariant (F04-7, F03-9). `consults` stays sorted by n. Inside one panel a lineage
     appears once (same provider + model is refused), and across runs the task lock serialises
     lineages, so "highest n of a lineage = newest thread" holds; `Select-ParentThread` unchanged.
     Stated in README and asserted by a harness case (slowest member first in roster order).

D11. Guard from the spec (F04-6). The parent's kill guard for a member = its timeout + the format
     repair and denial retry budgets (when enabled) + 60 s write lock + 120 s slack.

D12. Task lock for the whole panel stays (F03-8 accepted as a limitation): `codex-findings.ps1`
     writes are refused while a panel runs, as a single run refuses them today. D2 makes relaxing
     this later (R12) safe. Documented.

D13. Fakes (F03-10): a per-model delay map and per-model reply for fake-codex3 (keyed by `-m`) and a
     delay for fake-agy, before the panel cases.
